The First Chapter

The keeper climbed the stairs every evening and lit the *great* lamp before the fishing boats came home. He kept a careful record of the weather in a notebook that he called the **Ledger**, and nobody else was allowed to read it.

The Ledger

Its pages were full of small, neat handwriting. Some entries were *underlined twice*, and one of them, from a winter long ago, was marked **urgent** in red ink beside the date.

[Figure: The harbour wall at low tide, seen from the lighthouse.]

The Winter Entry

Nobody in the village could explain what had happened that winter, although everyone had a story about it.

The Second Chapter

In the spring the schoolteacher asked to see the notebook. The keeper said **no** at first, but he changed his mind after she told him about the *Mariner*, a ship her grandfather had sailed on.

What They Found

Together they read the winter entry again, slowly, and this time the words made sense to both of them.
